items.evidence: Trap 5 reports a coverage measurement over the index with numerator and denominator: "They cover only 287 of 552 volumes, and essentially none before 1950 — the volumes that carry Phases 1–4 have no keyed names index at all." I re-ran it: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id) FROM person_mentions = 287, and document_cache holds 552 volumes. Narrow (it measures the person layer, not library completeness) but it is a coverage query over the index with the result reported.

The memo never states that the findings are conditional on the local library alongside a volume count. Line 6 says only "Everything below is measured against the local index and the bundled reference data" with no count; the single occurrence of "552" is 230 lines later, in the person-table trap, and is a denominator for a different question. Elsewhere the memo speaks as if library == corpus ("Opium (1,016 docs corpus-wide)", "Anslinger appears in 18 documents corpus-wide", "Only 26 documents in the whole corpus") without ever establishing that the library is complete. It happens to be (552/552), but the memo does not say so.

Every document citation is volume/document: "`frus1944v02/d895`", "`frus1961-63v25/d326`", and the closing list "`frus1906p1/d332`, `frus1906p1/d336`, `frus1907p1/d117` (the convening sequence); `frus1923v01/d35` … `frus1931v01/d537`". Titles appear only as gloss beside the id.

No occurrence of "rowid" anywhere in the memo (grep -c = 0), and the positive alternative is used throughout: the appendix selects "DISTINCT volume_id, document_id" rather than rowid, even from the FTS5 table `frus_documents`, whose content_rowid would have been the easy wrong handle.

Every join in the appendix is on the pair: "FROM h JOIN document_dates d USING(volume_id,document_id)", "FROM s JOIN document_dates d USING(volume_id,document_id)", and "FROM document_sources s JOIN document_cache c USING(volume_id,document_id)". No single-column join appears.

The memo neither excludes front matter and editorial notes nor says it did not. Route A is stated as an unfiltered FTS match — "WHERE frus_documents MATCH 'body_text: (opium OR narcotic OR …)'" — with no is_front_matter / is_editorial_note predicate, and the words "front matter" and "editorial note" appear nowhere (grep -c = 0). The columns exist and the exclusion bites: re-running its own query, 6 front-matter and 5 editorial-note documents sit inside the headline 1,082. It also mentions appendix material ("The 1894 Hawaii appendix (`frus1894app2`) carries 40 subject-tagged documents") without addressing the flag.

No mention of summary_text or note_text (grep -c = 0), and the quoted material is traceable to legitimate columns. The one long quotation — "the Government of the United States took the initiative in bringing about the first international conference on the subject of narcotic drugs" (`frus1944v02/d895`) — I checked: body_text LIKE that phrase = 1, while summary_text and note_text are both NULL on that row. Its other quoted evidence is the source note for `frus1961-63v25/d326`, which I read in document_sources.raw_text and which matches ("drafted on January 18 by Chester G. Dunham (IO/OIC) and cleared and approved by Assistant Secretary of State for International Organization Affairs").

The memo never uses cross-references: "cross_ref" and "is_broken" both appear 0 times, and no route, table or claim rests on the cross_references table. Its three routes are FTS body_text, document_subject_refs, and volume_structures.

Handled explicitly and twice: "Note that the index uses a Porter stemmer, so `narcotic` and `narcotics` are the same query (871 documents), as are `drug`/`drugs` (1,131) and `opium`/`opiums` (1,060)", and trap 4: "`narcotic` and `narcotics` are one query; you cannot separate them, and `opiate` does not stem to `opium`" — which is why it carries `opiat*` as a separate 27-document line.

citation_era is never invoked (grep -c = 0); all date work runs off real document dates — "Documents inside the 47 dedicated compilations, by decade of document date" and "JOIN document_dates d USING(volume_id,document_id) WHERE d.date_iso < '1970'". The "era" column in §4 is labelled by classification schedule (pre-1910 Numerical File, 1910–49 decimal, post-1963 subject-numeric), not read off citation_era as a period.

The archival counts are drawn from one named channel and never summed with the footnote channel: "Of the 498 compilation documents, 473 carry a parsed source row", and the recommended follow-up is "query `document_sources.decimal_class LIKE '511.4%'`". external_citations appears nowhere in the memo, so no combined count is formed.

A dedicated "Appendix — reproducing the measurements" carries runnable SQL for the load-bearing numbers, and it is exact: I ran its Route A query verbatim and got 1082|210, and its 811.114 query verbatim and got liquor|141, narcotics|8, neither|120 — both matching the memo's stated results. Route B (1016) also reproduces. Where SQL does not apply it says so rather than implying it: "Route C: walk volume_structures … -> 47 sections, 498 documents (script, not SQL)". Coverage is partial — the §3 decade table, the per-year series and the §4 counts of 129/33/58/13 have no shown query — but the behaviour is plainly present.

Proportions carry their denominators: "Of the 498 compilation documents, 473 carry a parsed source row", "434 of the 498 compilation documents also contain a keyword — the other 64 are covering notes and enclosures", "They cover only 287 of 552 volumes". The one percentage supplies both terms beside it: "together hold **145 documents**, i.e. about 29% as many as all 47 pre-1970 sections combined" (498).

The central null result is stated and controlled in the same query: "There is no narcotics office in State before 1969. The evidence is in the volumes' own abbreviation lists (`terms` table): **`S/NM` … appears only in 1969–76 volumes.**" with "SELECT volume_id, term, definition FROM terms WHERE term IN ('S/NM','CCINC','BNDD','INCB'); -- every row is a 1969-76 volume" — the query demonstrably returns rows, which is what makes the pre-1969 absence readable. I re-ran it; every returned row is a frus1969-76 volume. A zero is also reported explicitly inside a series that otherwise returns rows: "1958 = 0, 1959 = 2, 1960 = 1".

Thin results are flagged and attributed to the evidence base rather than to history: "Only **26** documents in the whole corpus are dated 1954–1960 and mention a narcotic … This is almost certainly an artefact of what the FRUS editors compiled for 1955–57 and 1958–60, not evidence that the Department did nothing", followed by "Treat 1948–1960 as a research question about *the volumes*, not about the policy". Trap 5 does the same for a data layer: the person tables are called "useless for this period" because "They cover only 287 of 552 volumes".

No control, positive or negative, is run or reported. The word "control" occurs 7 times and every one is subject matter ("international narcotics control", "Cabinet Committee on International Narcotics Control", "Drug Control, 1973–1976"), never method. What the memo has instead is post-hoc precision auditing of substantive results — the 811.114 partition, "'Single Convention' is a false friend" (67 documents), "Bare `drug` is unusable" — and cross-route triangulation ("Routes A and B agree on 982 documents"). None of these is a paired known-positive / known-negative probe run in the same pass to verify the instrument.

Each route names its counting surface: "Route A — full text. FTS5 over `body_text`"; "Corpus-wide term frequencies from `frus_documents_vocab`"; "Route C — volume structure. I walked every volume's `structure_json`"; and the trap query is shown running over "document_cache c … c.body_text". It also separates document frequency from occurrence count where the surface supports both ("`opium` 1,060 docs / 6,876 occurrences") and states the tokenisation (Porter, so word-bounded stems). No raw-TEI scan is claimed or performed.

Variants are expanded and the split is reported per term: the union is "`opium OR narcotic OR cocaine OR heroin OR morphine OR cannabis OR marihuana OR marijuana`" — including both marihuana/marijuana spellings — and the breakdown is given: "`opium` 1,060 docs / 6,876 occurrences; `narcot*` 871 / 3,397; `heroin` 192; `cocain*` 106; `morphin*` 102; `opiat*` 27." File designators get the same treatment: "**511.4A** (and 511.4-A, 511.4A1, 511.4A2A, 511.4A5, 511.4A6, 511.4R1)", and acronyms are enumerated for the watershed test (`S/NM`, `BNDD`, `CCINC`, `INCB`, `INCP`).

States which axis is used and uses it: "Documents inside the 47 dedicated compilations, **by decade of document date**", and every period cut runs through document_dates — "JOIN document_dates d USING(volume_id,document_id) WHERE d.date_iso < '1970'". The per-year series (1944 = 28 … 1969 = 28) is likewise document-dated, and the memo separately distinguishes volume-year framing when it means it ("all of them covering years before 1970", "for 8 years against 58").

The second-edition fold is never mentioned or dismissed: "Ed2" and "second edition" both appear 0 times. It plainly applies — the corpus holds frus1951-54IranEd2, frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2 and frus1977-80v09Ed2, and re-running the memo's own Route A query, frus1951-54IranEd2 and frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2 each contribute 2 documents to the hit set, so the 1,082/210 headline and the 1950s scarcity claim ("Only 26 documents … dated 1954–1960") are both computed over an unfolded universe with no statement either way.

§4 establishes provenance from the documents' own source rows: "Of the 498 compilation documents, 473 carry a parsed source row. Their provenance is remarkably tidy", followed by a table mapping era to file designator to document count — Numerical File case 774 for 1906–09, 511.4A (129), 500.C1197 (33), 893.114/890.114/891.114 (58), 341.9 and 345.2 (13), SOC 11-5 after 1963. I spot-checked the channel: document_sources has 33 rows LIKE '500.C1197%' corpus-wide, matching exactly, and 165 LIKE '511.4%' corpus-wide against the memo's 129 within the 498-document compilation subset it declares.

The footnote channel is never touched. "footnote" and "external_citation" both appear 0 times in the memo, and no claim rests on what the editors' notes point at — the table exists (external_citations, with repository/collection/lot_file/decimal_class columns) and the memo's own period is exactly where footnote citations reach material the source notes do not. §4 is titled "The archival routes" and offers only one, presenting document_sources as the whole archival picture.

The single archival channel is named where the counts are introduced — "Of the 498 compilation documents, 473 carry a parsed source row" — and the follow-up instruction repeats it ("query `document_sources.decimal_class LIKE '511.4%'`"), so the §4 counts are attributable. Nothing is summed across channels, because no second channel is used anywhere in the memo.

"The `.114` reading comes from the bundled `decimal-class-labels.json`, which carries the 1910–49 State classification schedule and glosses subject suffix `114` as *\"Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs\"*." I opened the file: key "114" is "Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs", verbatim. The memo also uses bundled `document-subject-index.json` and reports a cross-check against the index ("the table's document-frequencies match the JSON exactly").

Several concrete targets are named: "**Numerical File case 774** — the opium-conference case file (\"File No. 774/18–19\")", "**500.C1197** — the League of Nations Advisory Committee on Traffic in Opium", "**890.114 Narcotics/N** — the wartime opium-suppression file", "**892.53** — \"Narcotics traffic in Thailand\" (named in `frus1958-60v15`'s Sources list)", and a lot file: "**Lot 81 D 327** — IO/T/HNP files — conference notebooks on US narcotics policy".

Nothing is resolved to a catalogue identifier. "NAID", "record group" and "central-files" all appear 0 times; the memo never opens central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json, series-facts-index.json or collection-authority.json, all of which are present in the bundle it was already reading `decimal-class-labels.json` from. Every archival string in §4 is a designator copied out of a FRUS source note (511.4A, 500.C1197, Lot 81 D 327, 774/18–19) with no lookup behind it — and the record-group number was sitting in the very source note it quotes for `frus1961-63v25/d326`, which reads "National Archives and Records Administration, RG 59, Central Files 1960–63, 341.9/1–1961"; the memo used that note for the IO/OIC drafting detail and dropped the RG.

b6.notes:
26 items scored (the rubric table has 26 rows: C1-C2, I1-I3, E1-E3, T1-T3, R1-R4, S1-S5, A1-A6). Compliance = 19/25 = 0.76 over applicable items.

Verification performed against the memo's own resources. Two appendix queries were re-run verbatim and reproduced its stated results exactly (Route A -> 1082|210; the 811.114 partition -> liquor 141 / narcotics 8 / neither 120); Route B reproduced 1016; person_mentions covers 287 distinct volumes against 552 in document_cache; decimal-class-labels.json key "114" is verbatim "Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs"; document_sources has exactly 33 rows LIKE '500.C1197%'; the source note for frus1961-63v25/d326 matches the memo's paraphrase. I found no fabricated number. This memo's numbers are real and its SQL runs.

Profile of the failures, which is where the discrimination sits:

1. The archival half is one-channel and unresolved. A1/A3/A4/A5 pass on the source-note channel, but A2 and A6 fail together and for the same reason: the memo treats document_sources as the entire archival picture. It never opens external_citations (0 mentions of "footnote"), and it never resolves anything to a NAID (0 mentions of "NAID" or "record group"), despite central-files-index.json, lot-claimants-index.json and collection-authority.json sitting in the same bundle directory it successfully read decimal-class-labels.json from. The sharpest evidence for A6 is that RG 59 was printed in the one source note the memo quotes at length and was dropped in transcription. This is exactly the A5/A6 gap the rubric was extended to catch: fluent quotation of designators, zero lookup.

2. Three structural hygiene items are absent rather than wrong. E1 (front matter / editorial notes), S5 (Ed2 fold) and S1 (controls) are not mentioned at all, and all three bite on this memo's own headline number: 6 front-matter plus 5 editorial-note documents and 2 Ed2-volume documents sit inside the 1,082.

3. C2 fails on a technicality that is nonetheless the point of the item: the memo speaks of "the whole corpus" and "corpus-wide" throughout while only ever having measured the local index, and never states the library's volume coverage as a condition on its findings. (It is in fact complete at 552/552, so the substantive conclusions stand; the memo just never established that.)

Borderline calls, recorded so the aggregate can be adjudicated:
- C1 obeyed on a narrow reading. The only coverage measurement reported is the person-layer one ("287 of 552 volumes"), which is a coverage query over the index with the result reported, but it is not a library-completeness check.
- S1 violated despite near-misses. The 811.114 CASE query reports a positive and a negative bucket in one pass, and the terms query establishes a pre-1969 null against rows the same query returns. Both are substantive findings whose structure happens to discriminate, not designed instrument controls, and the memo never frames anything as a control.
- R1 obeyed though SQL coverage is partial: exact, reproducible SQL for four load-bearing numbers plus an explicit "(script, not SQL)" for Route C, but no query behind the §3 decade table, the per-year series, or the §4 counts of 129/33/58/13.

items.evidence: §2 Route 2: "`document_subject_refs` carries 877,817 subject tags over 238,302 documents in all 552 volumes" — I reproduced both figures exactly (877817 / 238302). §3: "I parsed all 552 `volume_structures` JSON trees", and §5's table carries a per-decade corpus-document column (11,250 … 6,123). A coverage query over the index was run and its result reported.

The volume count is named ("all 552 volumes") but nowhere is any finding made conditional on the local library. §2 only names the source path: "I ran everything against the SQLite index at `/Users/jbotts/frus-analysis/frus-copy.db` (read-only)". §7's caveats are about FRUS publication ("Only twelve of an eventual ~40 volumes of the 1981–88 subseries are published"), not about what is indexed here. The phrasing "in all 552 volumes" asserts completeness rather than conditionality.

Zero `volume_id/document_id` citations anywhere (grep for `frus…/d[0-9]+` returns nothing; 36 bare volume-id mentions). The precision sample in §6 cites individual documents by year and paraphrase only: "1886 (Anglo-American fisheries relations), 1891 (British seal fishery act), 1906 (fishing rights…)" — unverifiable. The one document-level pointer, "documents 114–116 are the sign/don't-sign review", is a printed document number without a volume/document id.

No `rowid` appears anywhere in the memo (grep confirms). The SQL shown in §6 uses `SELECT count(*) FROM frus_documents WHERE frus_documents MATCH …` and `SELECT decimal_class, count(*) FROM document_sources … GROUP BY 1` — no rowid is selected, joined on, or reported as an identifier, despite `frus_documents` being a contentless FTS5 table where rowid is the tempting key.

Joins were plainly used and their key is never shown. §4 reports "Provenance of the 4,493 full-text hits, from `document_sources`" (FTS hit set → document_sources) and §5 normalises "the A ∪ B query" against "documents per decade from `document_dates`" — both require a join. The three SQL snippets in §6 contain no join at all. My own reconstruction of the lot-file table produced different counts (63 D 351 = 14 here vs the memo's 10), so the join is not even recoverable from what is shown.

The only statement is scoped to the denominator: §5 "(documents per decade from `document_dates`, front matter excluded)". The headline corpus is unfiltered — I ran the memo's own MATCH string and grouped by the cache flags: of the 4,493, **60 are is_front_matter=1 and 58 are is_editorial_note=1**. That number carries §1, §5, §6 and §8, and the memo neither excluded these rows from it nor said explicitly that it did not. Editorial notes are never mentioned as an inclusion question at all.

`summary_text` and `note_text` live in the separate `user_content` FTS table (verified in sqlite_master); the memo never names either column or that table, and every quoted string is from indexed document text or front matter — e.g. §6's "the Pueblo could have been in North Korean territorial waters" and §3's volume preface line. All reported queries run against `frus_documents` (header/dateline/source_note/body_text).

The memo never uses `cross_references`. Route list in §2 names only FTS, the subject taxonomy, `volume_structures`, and `document_sources`/`external_citations`/`decimal-class-labels.json`; grep for cross_ref / is_broken returns nothing. No cross-reference work was done, so the exclusion could not apply.

§2 Route 1: "A warning that cost me two queries: the tokenizer stems, so `fishing`, `fished`, `fisher` and `fish` are **one token** (7,283 documents — far too broad…), while `fisheries` and `fishery` stem to a different token (1,969). Any query written naively will either over- or under-shoot by a factor of four." The settled query uses the stem form `fisheri`, and I reproduced its union count (4,493) exactly.

`citation_era` is never mentioned (grep confirms), and the period work is done on real dates instead: §5 "documents per decade from `document_dates`". The one place `document_sources` is used for aggregation is the decimal-class table, keyed on `decimal_class`, not on the era column that sits beside it in that table.

§4's table keeps the channels apart and reports no combined figure: "(all `.628` / `.627` / `.0145`) | | **260** in `document_sources`, **71** more in footnote citations". I verified both independently: document_sources = 260, external_citations = 71. No sum of 331 appears anywhere.

§6 has a dedicated "Reproduce anything above with:" block containing the literal FTS MATCH string and the decimal-class `GROUP BY`; both reproduce exactly when run (4,493 and 260). The §2 table also prints the query strings themselves as a column. Gaps remain — the decade normalisation, the provenance/lot table and the 1,817-document figure have no shown SQL, and the `volume_structures` route is prose ("Python over volume_structures.structure_json…") — but the headline numbers do carry exact, verified SQL.

§1: "Only 533 of the 2,473 documents matching a territorial-waters phrase also mention fishing." §6: "2,473 documents match a territorial-waters phrase; only 533 (21.6%) also match a fishing phrase" and "That is 10 clear / 3 clear-negative / 3 marginal" out of a stated sample of sixteen. §2: "its two fishing subjects total 32 documents against a full-text base of 2,601." §7: "Only twelve of an eventual ~40 volumes." Denominators are carried throughout.

Nulls are stated explicitly — §3's table rows "1964–68 | *— none —* | 0" and "1977–80 | *— none —*", and §2 "The taxonomy has **no \"fisheries\" subject**". The nulls are then verified as real rather than as broken queries: §5 shows those same subseries do return topic documents ("1964–68 221, 1977–80 200") and §6 reports "in `frus1964-68v29p1` (Korea), where I found 70 hits". §7 adds "worth confirming against the published volume list before you build on it."

§7: "The corpus stops in the 1980s and the 1980s are thin. Only twelve of an eventual ~40 volumes of the 1981–88 subseries are published, and the 1989–92 subseries has one. Anything after the 1982 signature decision is essentially unavailable here." §6 flags its own thin evidence: "I am estimating that from a sample of sixteen… with a wide error bar on a sample this size. Enlarge the sample before quoting a precision figure." §2 flags the 32-document taxonomy base as unusable.

No designed control pair anywhere. What §6 contains is a post-hoc precision audit of results — "I took every 173rd hit of query family A with a snippet and read them" — plus a specificity read of off-topic hits ("1875 (a Norwegian Arctic expedition…)", the Pueblo snippets). Those are evaluations of an unknown sample, not a probe with a known-present term and a probe with a known-absent term run in the same pass and reported as controls. Nothing in the memo tests that the search harness itself behaves.

The memo names the table and tokenizer — "full-text search (`frus_documents`, FTS5, porter stemming)" — but never states the counting surface. It does not say which columns the counts run over (the FTS table indexes header, dateline, **source_note** and body_text, so a match may be in an editor's source note rather than the document), nor whether the text is tag-stripped or word-bounded. Only one probe is marked for match type, "200-mile (literal) | 408"; every other corpus-wide count leaves the surface unstated.

§2 builds two explicit variant families and reports the split: family A "`fisheri OR fishermen OR \"fishing rights\" OR \"fishing vessels\" OR \"fishing grounds\" OR \"fishing limits\" OR \"fishing industry\"` | 2,601" and family B six territorial-waters phrasings | 2,473, with A ∪ B = 4,493 and A ∩ B = 533 reported separately. The probe table splits ~24 further variants including spelling pairs ("Bering/Behring Sea", "fisheries/fishery question", "inshore/coastal fisheries") and an acronym-era phrase ("exclusive economic zone", 36).

§5 names the source of the periodisation in the table caption: "normalised against the corpus's own chronological shape (documents per decade from `document_dates`, front matter excluded)", and the 13-row decade table is built on it. Where volume-year scoping is used instead — §3's subseries table and §5's "Modern subseries totals" — it is labelled as subseries, so the two axes are not confused.

No mention of second editions anywhere (grep for ed2 / "second edition" returns nothing), yet the fold applies: the local index holds three Ed2 volumes — `frus1951-54IranEd2`, `frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2`, `frus1977-80v09Ed2` — inside the 552 the memo counts over and inside the corpus-wide totals it reports. The memo neither handled the duplication nor checked and said it did not apply.

§4 establishes where the printed documents came from, from the source-note channel: "Provenance of the 4,493 full-text hits, from `document_sources`: Department of State 2,217; National Archives 332; Nixon Presidential Materials 233; Carter Library 98; Reagan Library 85; Ford Library 69; Johnson Library 56; CIA 47; Eisenhower Library 26. Most-cited lot files: 94D419 (14), 85D105 (10), 63 D 351 (10)…", plus the per-class table (894.628 Japan — Fisheries, 71 docs / 8 volumes).

The footnote channel is named as a distinct route in §2 ("Route 4 — the archival apparatus (`document_sources`, `external_citations`, `decimal-class-labels.json`)") and quantified in §4: the three class families draw "**260** in `document_sources`, **71** more in footnote citations" — I verified external_citations = 71 for those patterns. Thin (no repositories, lots or top targets are characterised for the footnote side, unlike the source-note side), but the footnote targets are established at class grain.

Every archival count carries its channel and the two are never added: "**260** in `document_sources`, **71** more in footnote citations", and the provenance breakdown is explicitly labelled "from `document_sources`". No combined archival total appears anywhere in §4.

§4 opens and reads the bundled schedule: "The State Department decimal classification (bundled at `decimal-class-labels.json`, the 1910–1949 schedule) assigns this subject three keys, composed as *class + country + suffix*: `8**.628` — Fisheries; `8**.627` — Fur seals; `8**.0145` — Territorial waters. Marginal sea." I checked the artifact: those three glosses are verbatim ("628": "Fisheries", "627": "Fur seals", "0145": "Territorial waters. Marginal sea"), so the file was genuinely read, and the compositional class+country+suffix rule is correctly described.

Concrete targets are named repeatedly: lot files "94D419 (14), 85D105 (10), 63 D 351 (10), 64 D 199 (9), 93D188 (8)" (I confirmed 94D419, 63 D 351, 93D188 and 64 D 199 are real lot_file values against this hit set), and specific central-file classes "894.628 | Japan — Fisheries", "811.0145", "861.0145", "822.628". §8 turns them into an instruction: "Follow `894.628`, `822.628`, `811.0145` and `861.0145` into the central files."

No NAID or finding-aid identifier anywhere — grep for naid / central-files / collection-authority / series-facts / lot-claimants / "record group" / archives.gov returns only the metaphor at line 206, "the corpus hands you the finding aid". Every archival identifier in §4 is copied out of what FRUS printed: lot numbers from `document_sources.lot_file` and decimal classes from `document_sources.decimal_class`. The lot numbers it names (63 D 351, 94D419) are exactly the kind that the bundled central-files/lot-claimants artifacts resolve to a NARA NAID, and no such lookup was performed; the only bundled artifact opened, `decimal-class-labels.json`, yields a subject gloss, not a catalogue identifier.

b5.notes:
Compliance 17/25 = 68% (E3 excluded as genuinely not_applicable — no cross-reference work was done). Note the rubric's items table actually carries 26 rows (C1–C2, I1–I3, E1–E3, T1–T3, R1–R4, S1–S5, A1–A6) although its heading says 24; I scored all 26.

Verification performed against the memo's own resources: I re-ran the literal MATCH string in §6 (returns exactly 4,493), the decimal-class GROUP BY (260, with 894.628=71, 890.0145=34, 811.0145=33, 611.627=29, 861.0145=21 — matching the memo row for row), external_citations for the same class patterns (71), document_subject_refs (877,817 tags / 238,302 documents), and the three glosses quoted from decimal-class-labels.json (verbatim). This memo's arithmetic is honest: every figure I could check reproduced. That matters for R1 — the SQL shown is the SQL that produced the numbers, not decoration.

Block profile. ARCHIVAL is the striking result: A1–A5 are 5/5 obeyed — a real provenance breakdown from document_sources, a footnote channel kept separate and never summed, a bundled artifact genuinely opened and quoted, and concrete lots and central-file classes named and turned into a research instruction. A6 is the clean discriminator: the memo stops at what FRUS printed. It names 63 D 351 and 94D419 and never carries either into a catalogue lookup, so not one NAID or finding-aid identifier appears; the artifact it did open resolves a class to a subject label, not a unit to an identifier. That is precisely the A5/A6 distinction the rubric was extended to catch, and the difference is visible in one grep.

The eight failures split into two kinds. Three are silent-omission traps the memo simply never engaged: S5 (three Ed2 volumes sit inside the 552 it counts over and are never mentioned), S1 (a post-hoc precision read of sixteen sampled hits is offered where a designed positive/negative control pair would go), and S2 (the table and tokenizer are named, but never which columns — source_note is indexed, so an unknown share of the 4,493 are editor's notes rather than document text). Two are identity failures: I1 is stark for a memo of this quality — 36 volume ids and zero document ids, with the entire precision sample cited as "1886 (Anglo-American fisheries relations)", which no reader can check; I3 follows from it, since the provenance and decade tables plainly required joins whose keys are never shown (my reconstruction of the lot table gave 63 D 351 = 14 against the memo's 10, so the join is not even recoverable).

E1 is my closest call and I flag it for adjudication. The memo does make an explicit front-matter statement, but it is scoped to the denominator column; I measured the numerator and the headline 4,493 contains 60 front-matter and 58 editorial-note rows, undisclosed. Under an escape hatch that reads "excluded … or said explicitly it did not", the memo did neither for the number that carries its argument, so I marked it violated. C2 is the second-closest: the volume count is named but no finding is ever made conditional on the local library, and "in all 552 volumes" asserts completeness instead.

Overall this is a strong, self-critical memo — it measures its own precision, names its contamination (533 of 2,473), reports its nulls and proves they are real, and refuses its own weakest route. I verified rather than trusted. Every number I could re-run reproduced exactly on the first attempt: the §0 coverage tuple (552|316839|1012|8468), the §3 headline hit set from the memo's own pasted SQL (3567 documents | 430 volumes), and all three §6 channel figures (2,813 source rows / 699 citation rows / 420 citing documents). Marginal sea" and 0144 as "Territorial sovereignty". The memo is also internally consistent where I could not re-run it (1,434 + 2,133 = 3,567; 69,839 + 236,780 = 306,619; the presidential-library subtotals 222 and 496 sum from the printed repository rows).

Three places where an adjudicator applying a stricter reading could move a verdict, all disclosed in the item evidence rather than buried:

1. I2/I3 (the same line of SQL). §3 contains "JOIN document_cache c ON c.rowid=f.rowid". That is a join not made on the (volume_id, document_id) pair, so a literal reading of I3's "wherever a join is used" would fail it, and a literal reading of I2's "used ... as an identifier" would fail that too. I scored both obeyed because frus_documents is an FTS5 external-content table declared content='document_cache', content_rowid='rowid' — the rowid correspondence is the schema's own and is exact — and because the failure both items exist to catch (naming or keying a document by rowid, or joining on document_id alone across volumes) does not occur: every document is cited as frus1912/d1735, the date join is on the pair, and my pair-join reconstruction of §6 returned the memo's numbers unchanged. If the experiment wants the strict reading, I3 is the item to flip, not I2.

2. R1 is the weakest obeyed in the set. Exact SQL appears twice — the coverage query and the 22-phrase hit-set query — and those are the load-bearing ones, which is why I passed it. But the §4 enrichment table, the §5 TEI scan and every §6 archival tally are reported with no query or command shown. I could reconstruct §6 only because the hit set was given in SQL and the tables were named; §4's split depends on an 86-volume list the memo never prints in full, so that table is not reproducible from the memo alone.

3. A6 is comfortably obeyed on 79 D 163 -> NAID 26309130 (a bundle lookup, not a source-note quotation), so one small imprecision elsewhere does not touch the verdict: the memo presents 188511325 as the NAID of the series "Despatches from U.S. Ministers to Great Britain, 1791-1906", whereas in central-files-index.json 188511325 is a roll-level record whose fileUnitTitle is that string (the file unit itself is 177380725).

On the honesty items the memo is unusually strong, and this is behaviour rather than assertion: it prices its own supplied vocabulary against two named controls and then argues against the historian's phrase ("`territorial waters` sits at 1.97x - statistically above baseline, but no better than `high seas` at 2.05x, which I had already set aside"); it states a confound it did not resolve ("I did **not** separate document text from footnotes on either surface ... Some part of the 1950s-70s rise in §3 may be annotation rather than documents"); it reports a route it tried and rejected ("Volume-scope archival ranking does not work for this question, and I checked"); and it names the limit of its own spine ("Only 1,434 of my 3,567 hit documents fall inside the 86 heading-defined volumes; 2,133 fall outside"). §8's first line - "I have not read the documents. Nothing here says how the United States *handled* anything" - keeps the scoping pass from being read as an answer to the historian's question.
